== General Information ==
'''Haplogroup R-S14827'''represents a significant node in the '''North Sea Germanic'''family tree. Formed roughly around '''350 CE''', it corresponds with the final phase of the Roman Iron Age and the beginning of the Migration Period in Europe. 

This haplogroup serves as the parent to both modern Scandinavian lines (who remained in the Nordic homeland) and the "Proto-Norman" lines (who migrated south, eventually forming the [[Space:R-FT4811|R-FT4811]] lineage).

=== The Migration Period (c. 350 CE) ===
As the Roman Empire collapsed, the stability of Northern Europe shifted, leading to the "Völkerwanderung" or Great Migration. This era saw significant movements of Germanic tribes, including the Angles, Saxons, and Jutes, as well as the early expansion of Norse populations.

Genetic evidence indicates a major split in the R-S14827 lineage during this volatile era:

* '''The "Stay-at-Homes" (R-BY136156):''' 
One branch of the family remained in Scandinavia. Their descendants are found today primarily in Sweden and Norway, confirming the geographic origin of the clan.
** '''DNA Matches:'''
*** '''[[Andersson-4118|Lars Andersson (abt.1700-)]]''' (Sweden).
*** '''[[Carlsen-157|Carl Frederik Wilhelm Carlsen (abt.1812-1842)]]''' (Norway).
** ''Significance:'' These matches act as a "genetic anchor," proving that the ancestors of the Glasgow/Churnside families originated in Scandinavia before their migration to Britain.

* '''The "Migrants" (The Path to R-FT4811):''' 
The parallel branch left Scandinavia. While their exact path is lost to history, genetic distribution suggests they joined the '''Danish/Jute migrations''' into England or the early '''Norse raids''' into Northern France (Normandy). This branch eventually produced the "Grandfather Ancestor" ([[Space:R-FT4811|R-FT4811]]) who arrived in Britain during the Norman Conquest.

== Research Analysis ==
The existence of R-BY136156 (The Swedish/Norwegian branch) is critical for the '''Glasgow Name Study'''because it rules out a Celtic or indigenous British origin for the lineage. It confirms that the family was originally Norse/Germanic and arrived in Britain as part of a specific migration event—most likely the Norman Conquest, given the timeline of the downstream mutation [[Space:R-FT4811|R-FT4811]].
